scope: Follow-up bug bash prompted by an agent's report of an expired connection and failing browser/search/file tools.

incident_evidence.source: Read-only inspection of local connection metadata and privacy-filtered action/timing records; no credentials or page contents retained here.
confirmed: The inspected recent Full control / Always grant was still valid.
Screen capture and screen-control calls in that session succeeded.
Two service-tool failures recorded browser_window_required and loading (the browser had not reached the exact requested page).
unresolved: The earlier expired connection could not be identified without its exact error or timestamp.
The newly reproduced transport and saved-expiry bugs are not proven causes of the reported incident.
No live Gmail retry or access to messages was performed.

findings.finding: CLI clients rejected valid owner-extended grants after the expiry saved in the original credential passed.
findings.evidence_before: Three remote-CLI regressions and three legacy credential-CLI regressions failed before their corresponding local expiry checks were removed. Even the expired/revoked cases failed to reach the authoritative server response.
findings.fix: Treat the saved deadline as a snapshot; Reach enforces the current grant expiry and revocation on every request.
findings.verified: An extended grant succeeds after the original deadline; expired and revoked grants still receive HTTP 401.

findings.finding: The advertised displayId screenshot route was not recognized as a binary image route by CLI transports.
findings.evidence_before: Three of four regression checks failed: direct HTTP and tailnet attempted to parse JPEG bytes as JSON for /api/browser/desktop/screen?maxWidth=2560&displayId=2.
findings.fix: Accept valid maxWidth/displayId combinations on the exact desktop screenshot route, while rejecting duplicate, unknown, malformed or lookalike parameters.

findings.finding: MCP screenshot JSON encoding exceeded ordinary transport budgets even when the image was within the existing 8 MiB binary limit.
findings.evidence_before: Both direct HTTP and tailnet rejected a synthetic 2 MiB image wrapped as MCP JSON with 'Reach response exceeds 2 MiB.' An 8 MiB image also needs more than the hosted/public-link 8 MiB JSON budget after base64 encoding.
findings.fix: Use a shared bounded base64-envelope budget only for successful exact MCP screenshot/app-screen calls, including one compact reach_execute wrapper. Integrate direct, tailnet, signed Funnel and hosted dispatch, and validate decoded image bytes.
findings.verified: An exact 8 MiB synthetic image passes full/compact calls; decoded 8 MiB + 1 byte is refused even when its encoded length is identical. Oversized ordinary responses, error responses and lookalike routes retain their prior limits.

findings.finding: The observed service-tool loading code lost its actionable recovery instructions at the connector boundary.
findings.evidence_before: Two of three fixed-message/privacy regressions failed because loading returned only generic live-page verification guidance.
findings.fix: Return a fixed loading message that asks the agent to check the chosen browser and account, wait for the exact page, and retry. Preserve the exact-page/account checks and never forward arbitrary native exception or page text.
findings.limit: This improves the observed failure's recovery guidance. It does not prove why Gmail failed to load or change its navigation rules.
